title: What If You Could See Winning Lottery Tickets?
description: Imagine knowing which lottery tickets are winners before buying them. A few hundred dollars turns into thousands... until you spot a ticket worth $250 MILLION. There's just one problem: someone else is reaching for it first. Getting rich should be easy with this superpower, right? But what if the biggest jackpot comes with a price nobody can see? Would you grab the ticket?
format: 16:9 long-form with thin black letterbox bars baked in (~5% top/bottom), 854x480 @30fps downloaded (<=480p), 16:32

analysis_notes.production_defect: 11:42-12:42 repeats the narration of 10:46-11:36 word for word (~51 s duplicated) while the picture holds on a single slow push-in 'phone recording' PiP for ~70 s. Cut rate collapses to 5/min in minute 12. A likely upload/edit error that a viewer would notice; the most obvious reason this control video sits at the channel median while the same-template IQ video (2TsZSQ77E9o) hit 4.4x.

art_style: Same ConChaser house style as 2TsZSQ77E9o: flat 2D vector 'black ball-head stickman'. Solid black circle heads with white oval eyes and eyebrow strokes (mouth only when talking or shocked), thin black limbs, a coloured clothing shape per character (protagonist = mustard-yellow hoodie; Jake = purple hoodie + headphones; rival = dark grey hoodie; cashier = red/orange shirt with braids; customer = red cap). Soft-shaded flat backgrounds with depth-of-field blur (convenience-store counter with colourful scratch-card display, street at night, car interior, apartment). Key props are bright and glowing: green neon '$250,000,000' price pills floating over tickets, a glowing green lottery terminal, red numbers for losses. Interstitial 'title cards' on dark gradient with big glowing green numbers (e.g. '$250,000,000', '9 HOURS', '43:00'), and dark-navy 'blueprint' diagram cards with thin cyan lines to explain the rules. Big-hand close-ups (black gloved hand pointing at / holding ticket) for tactile beats.
title_pattern: What If You Could See [hidden value] [on an everyday object]? -- channel template 'What If You Could See X?' (sibling: 'What If You Could See Everyone's IQ?'). Superpower = a floating number overlay on a mundane thing; the noun (Winning Lottery Tickets) carries the money promise. No number in the title; the $250M lives in the thumbnail.

thumbnail.composition: Low, counter-level 3/4 view across a store counter. Bottom-centre hero object: a scratch card outlined in glowing neon green. Left foreground: a large 3D-cartoon human (wide eyes, cap, dark hoodie) reaching his finger toward it. Right mid-ground: a black ball-head character in a mustard-yellow hoodie lunging in with an open gloved hand and angry eyebrows. Other scratch cards ('CASH BLAST', 'LUCKY 7') frame the hero ticket at both lower corners.
thumbnail.text: Only the in-world ticket text: '$250 MILLION' in big white bold type on the green ticket, plus a pseudo 'MEGA MILLIONS' logo. No overlay headline.
thumbnail.colours: Neon green glow (hero) vs warm amber/orange store lighting and red/orange side cards; saturated mustard-yellow hoodie as second focal point; dark hoodie/black head for contrast.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Ticket and reaching hand dominate the bottom half (huge, close to lens); two rivals converge on it from left and right, a two-hands-one-prize race. The black ball-head figure is mid-sized so the human's shocked face reads first.
thumbnail.why_it_works: One unmistakable prize with a glowing money number, a race (two hands, one ticket) that mirrors the cold open, and a shocked face for emotion. Weaknesses: it's a glossy 3D render that doesn't match the flat 2D video (the human character never appears), and the pseudo-logo text is garbled. That style mismatch may cost click-to-watch retention.

hook.first_5s_verbatim: $250 million. That's how much the lottery ticket sitting on the counter is worth. And the guy standing in front of you is about to buy it.
hook.first_30s_verbatim: $250 million. That's how much the lottery ticket sitting on the counter is worth. And the guy standing in front of you is about to buy it. You have exactly 3 seconds. 3 2 1. You sprint across the convenience store. Wait. The guy reaches for the ticket. You dive forward. Your hand flies over the counter. And just as your fingers are about to touch $250 million, the cashier picks it up. Sir, please stop running in the store.
hook.device: Cold open in medias res (flash-forward to the 7:00 climax), opened by a bare dollar number as the first two words, in second person ('you'), plus an on-screen countdown (3-2-1 ring) and a slow-motion dive. Then a comic deflation ('Sir, please stop running in the store'), then the premise is stated at 0:44 ('this morning you woke up with the ability to see the exact prize hidden inside every lottery ticket') and a 'quarter-billionaire' title card at 0:56. The video loops back explicitly at 7:22 ('that's where we started').
hook.visual: 0:00 glowing terminal with a '$250,000,000' pill over a blurred store; 0:02 push-in to the terminal; 0:10 black screen with a red 3-second countdown ring and a gloved hand; 0:20-0:24 slow-mo yellow-sleeved hand reaching toward a floating glowing ticket with bokeh.

beats.summary: A bare big number ($250M) on a glowing ticket; a rival is about to buy it.
3-second countdown, sprint, slow-motion dive; the cashier snatches the ticket away; comic deflation.
'Here's the thing': you can see the prize inside every ticket since this morning. 'Quarter-billionaire' title card.
7 AM energy-drink run; a red '$0' floats over a disputed scratch card; you test the power on a $500 card, pay $5, and it pays exactly $500.
Skip class, hop between stores, small wins ($1,000, $5,000); comic lunch splurge ('even paid for guacamole'), 'basically a billionaire'.
Bigger numbers ($50k, $200k); a TV ad for tonight's $250M jackpot sets the goal.
The jackpot ticket is somewhere in the city: 83 retailers, 9 hours until the drawing. Starts running.
Store-hopping disappoints; you discover the big numbers float over unissued quick-pick entries and shift until purchase. A diagram explains it: right ticket + right moment. 8 hours left.
31 stores, phone dying, taxi costs; a $3M number at a gas station flickers; you order half a second too late, ticket prints $0.
6 hours left. Call best friend Jake ('Bro, I need your car' / '$250 million' / 'I'm listening'); a $5,000 ticket convinces him.
3 hours of driving; running gag 'Are we rich yet? No.'
A huge $250M number glows through a store window; 'Stop the car'; you burst in, a hooded guy is reaching for it, 'that's where we started'.
Cashier is annoyed; you bid $100, $200, $500 for the guy's ticket; the 'lucky number seven' lie fails; he counters at $2,000; deal.
For one second you hold $250M, then the number flips to $0. Jake sits on the floor; the rival walks off laughing with your $2,000.
Watch other customers' numbers stay stable; the receipt shows the cashier cancelled the original order and printed a new quick pick. The original numbers are gone, unless... Jake was recording.
Narration of 10:46-11:36 repeats verbatim over a static, slowly pushing-in phone-recording PiP. Production error, not a story beat.
Phone video: zoom in, six original numbers visible. 43 minutes until the drawing; the cashier enters them manually; the printer counts 1-2-3 seconds; $250M appears above it. 'Keep the change.'
In the car for 40 minutes: mansion, jet, supercars; Jake wants a yacht ('he couldn't swim... he'd learn').
Live draw, the numbers match one by one (ticket graphic lights green per number), the final number held; WIN, celebration gags (hugged a parking meter).

Unknown number calls: 'Congratulations... someone who used to have the same ability... you thought you were the only one.' A red '-$250,000,000' appears under the green number. 'You can see how much a ticket wins, but you haven't learned how much it costs.'
The same red -$250M number floats over Jake, the stranger, the cashier; you're not sure you want to cash it.
'If you knew a ticket would win you $250 million, but you had no idea what the real price would be, would you still buy it?' End card 'WOULD YOU STILL BUY IT?'.

pacing.cut_detection: ffmpeg scene>0.3 on 320px proxy; counts visual changes (cuts, card slams, value-pill swaps)
pacing.notes: Steady 20-28 changes/min through setup and hunt, peaking at 37/min in the negotiation (minute 7). It drops to 9/min in the receipt investigation and 5/min in the duplicated PiP stretch (11:42-12:42), the dead spot. It recovers to 30/min for the live draw. Re-hooks roughly every 40-70 s: countdown timers (9 hours, 8 hours, 6 hours, 43:00, 40 minutes), new numbers ($3M, $250M), 'But something bothered you', 'Then you noticed...', a near-miss, the twist flip to $0. The hook runs long (56 s cold open + premise) before the origin story starts at 0:58.

techniques_worth_copying: Open on a bare number as the first spoken words ('$250 million.') and the first frame (a glowing number pill). The value is the hook.
Cold open flash-forward to the mid-video climax, then an explicit 'that's where we started' when the story catches up (7:22). It pays off the open and resets attention at the 45% mark.
Second-person narration ('you') turns the what-if into a simulation of the viewer; dialogue is reported by the same voice, so one TTS voice is enough.

Superpower rendered as one consistent UI element (floating rounded number pill, green = win, red = loss/cost) that can be multiplied over any object or person. The final twist only needs a colour change.
Visible ticking clock: big gold countdown title cards (9 HOURS, 8 HOURS, 43:00, 40 MINUTES) plus a persistent small red timer in the corner.
A rule-discovery mid-section that complicates the power (numbers shift until purchase) and is explained with a minimalist navy 'blueprint' diagram. Cheap to animate, raises stakes.
Comedy relief beats between tension beats: guacamole splurge, 'Are we rich yet? No.' running gag, failed 'lucky number seven' lie, hugging a parking meter.
Near-miss before the success ($3M ticket missed by '+0.5 s', shown as a timing bar graphic).
Reversal at ~55% (the bought ticket flips to $0), then a clever recovery (friend's phone recording reveals the cancelled numbers).
Number-by-number match reveal with a ticket card lighting green per ball, holding the last one ('And the final number is...').

Late twist that recontextualises the power (a mysterious caller with a voice-waveform visual; a red negative number under the prize) and spreads the dread to everyone around, then ends on a direct 'would you still...?' question for comments.
Running money tally chip ('WON TODAY: $X') in the corner during the montage.
Lesson from the defect: never let the picture stall. A 60 s static PiP over repeated narration halved the cut rate. Add a QA check for duplicated transcript spans and long static shots before upload.
code_only_remake_needs: Ball-head stickman SVG rig shared with the IQ-video kit: expression presets (neutral, side-eye, shocked O, squint, crying, smug grin), clothing shapes per character (yellow hoodie, purple hoodie + headphones, dark hoodie, cashier shirt + braids, red cap), poses (stand, walk/run cycle, point, reach/dive, hold phone, sit on floor, arms-up celebrate), mouth flap on dialogue.
Big gloved-hand close-up component (point, reach, hold ticket, hold phone, hand money, type keypad).
Value pill component: rounded dark pill with glowing green/red text, number tween/flicker (random values -> settle), stacking (green above red), attach to object or head, many instances at once.

Props: lottery terminal with glowing screen, printer slip emerging, quick-pick slip with number rows, scratch-card set (flat cards with names and prize amounts), receipt with highlighted rows, wallet, cash bills, phone (call screen, banking app, camera REC UI with scrub bar), lotto ball machine, wall clock, steering wheel.

Backgrounds (flat SVG with blur layer for depth of field): convenience-store counter with colourful scratch-card display (day + night variants and 4-5 storefront names), gas station, street day/night, car interior night, apartment, bedroom, diner counter, house and supercar daydream cutaways.
Title-card templates: dark gradient + glowing large number + small tracked caps label; gold countdown cards; red '$0' card; radial sunburst background for joy beats.
Navy blueprint diagram template: thin cyan line boxes, arrows with draw-on (stroke-dashoffset), labels.
Voice-waveform card (animated bars from TTS amplitude, colour per mood) with quoted caption, plus spotlight silhouette figure.
Camera: slow push-ins, snap zooms, radial focus rings for the slow-mo dive, PiP frame component for 'recorded video' replays (with the picture animating inside).
Overlays: persistent corner countdown timer, running 'WON TODAY' tally, caption chips with strike-through for rejected ideas ('LUCK', 'MEMORIZED THE NUMBERS').
Audio: single narrator TTS (~148 wpm), music bed with swells at reveals, SFX (printer, cash register, phone ring, whoosh, brake squeal, crowd cheer).
Pipeline QA: detect repeated transcript spans and shots longer than ~6 s without motion.
